exercises.title: Index the foreign key you join on
exercises.problemHtml:
Every report joins tblWorksOn to tblProject on proNum, but tblWorksOn's primary key starts with empSSN, so searching by proNum scans the table. Create an index named idx_workson_pronum on tblWorksOn(proNum).

FUHCompany schema (the course's sample database — full script in the FUHCompany.sql tab)
TableColumns (PK underlined, FK in italics)
tblEmployeeempSSN DECIMAL(18,0), empName NVARCHAR(50), empAddress NVARCHAR(100), empSalary DECIMAL(10,0), empSex CHAR(1) (F/M), empBirthdate DATE, depNum → tblDepartment, supervisorSSN → tblEmployee
tblDepartmentdepNum INT, depName NVARCHAR(50) UNIQUE, mgrSSN → tblEmployee, mgrAssDate DATE
tblProjectproNum INT, proName NVARCHAR(50), locNum → tblLocation, depNum → tblDepartment
tblWorksOnempSSN, proNum, workHours DECIMAL(5,1)
tblLocationlocNum INT, locName NVARCHAR(50) UNIQUE
tblDepLocationdepNum, locNum
tblDependentempSSN, depName NVARCHAR(50), depSex CHAR(1), depBirthdate DATE, depRelationship NVARCHAR(30)

14 employees, 5 departments, 6 projects, 16 work assignments, 5 dependents. Names are Vietnamese with diacritics; text compares case-insensitively as on SQL Server.

Requirements

  • CREATE INDEX idx_workson_pronum ON tblWorksOn (proNum); — the plain form runs on both SQL Server and PostgreSQL (NONCLUSTERED is the SQL Server default).

    empName        NVARCHAR(50)   NOT NULL,

exercises.problemHtml:
Table Orders(orderID PK, customerID, orderDate, status, total) with 5 million rows; status has 3 values. For each frequent query pick the most useful new index.

This set has 1 table. There is nothing to run: answer in the panel on the right and press Submit. Work each one out yourself first (on paper, or in SSMS on your own SQL Server), then check — every explanation after Submit says why the tempting wrong answer is wrong.

Requirements

  • Answer every question in the answer panel, then press Submit.
  • All answers must be correct to get Accepted; the explanation of every question appears after you submit.

solutionCodeJson.code:
# What an index costs — answer key

1. Finding one row among 1,000,000 with a B-tree index takes about how many page reads?Tìm một dòng trong 1.000.000 dòng bằng chỉ mục cây B tốn khoảng bao nhiêu lần đọc trang?
   Answer: c) 3–4 (the tree height)
   B-trees are very wide (hundreds of keys per page), so the height stays tiny: O(log n).VI: Cây B rất rộng (hàng trăm khoá mỗi trang) nên chiều cao rất nhỏ: O(log n).

2. A table has 8 indexes. One INSERT must…Một bảng có 8 chỉ mục. Một câu INSERT phải…
   Answer: b) write the row and update all 8 indexes
   Each index is a separate sorted structure to maintain on every write.VI: Mỗi chỉ mục là một cấu trúc sắp xếp riêng phải bảo trì mỗi lần ghi.

3. Which columns get an index automatically in SQL Server?Cột nào được SQL Server tự đánh chỉ mục?
   Answer: c) PRIMARY KEY and UNIQUE columns
   Foreign keys do NOT get one — add it yourself when you join on them.VI: Khoá ngoại KHÔNG được tự đánh — tự thêm khi bạn nối theo chúng.

4. Indexing every column "just in case" leads to…Đánh chỉ mục mọi cột "cho chắc" dẫn tới…
   Answer: b) slower writes and wasted storage, with little read benefit
   Index the columns your frequent queries filter, join or sort on — not all of them.VI: Đánh chỉ mục cột mà truy vấn thường xuyên lọc, nối hoặc sắp — không phải mọi cột.
